mechanism_narrative: The sharp recovery in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT from t-2w to t-0w signals more commuting and daytime exposure, which should keep RETAIL_REC rising over the next four weeks as trip chaining into shops and restaurants increases.
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT continue to rise for two more weeks but RETAIL_REC does not exceed its last-28-day mean by the end of four weeks, the mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL stays elevated while WORKPLACES remain depressed, discretionary outing capacity is constrained by time at home and retail visits fall further over the next two weeks, pushing RETAIL_REC downward.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL above 20 points while WORKPLACES below -40 points
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL remains above 20 and WORKPLACES remains below -40 but RETAIL_REC rises over the next two weeks, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A renewed drop in TRANSIT below the recent level indicates renewed mobility friction or discouragement, which should reduce spontaneous retail trips and lower RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -70 after being above -70 in the prior week
failure_condition: If TRANSIT crosses back below -70 yet RETAIL_REC does not decline relative to the last four-week mean within four weeks, the claim is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Because PARKS and GROCERY_PHARM have risen sharply from t-2w to t-0w, the city is experiencing broader out-of-home normalization; that spillover should continue lifting RETAIL_REC over the next week through near-term substitution from essential and leisure trips into shopping trips.
failure_condition: If PARKS and GROCERY_PHARM remain near their current levels but RETAIL_REC does not improve within one week, the mechanism fails.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained narrowing of the gap between RESIDENTIAL and WORKPLACES reflects normalization of daily routines, which should translate into a higher RETAIL_REC average over the next four weeks as households resume discretionary errands.
failure_condition: If the RESIDENTIAL-WORKPLACES gap narrows further but RETAIL_REC remains below its prior-28-day mean after four weeks, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A localized rebound in PARKS mobility should temporarily compete with retail time allocation; when PARKS rises above its recent plateau, retail activity softens over the next two weeks as outings are redirected outdoors.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by more than 15 points week-on-week
failure_condition: If PARKS rises by more than 15 points week-on-week and RETAIL_REC does not fall within two weeks, the mechanism is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM and TRANSIT both recover together, it indicates easing movement constraints and higher trip frequency; that combination should lift RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks as people bundle essential and discretionary trips.
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM and TRANSIT both stay above the stated thresholds but RETAIL_REC fails to improve over four weeks, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: The recent acceleration in WORKPLACES mobility relative to the slower improvement in RETAIL_REC implies a lagged catch-up effect; retail-and-recreation should rise over the next one to four weeks as commuting-driven foot traffic converts into shopping visits.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES increases for two consecutive weeks while RETAIL_REC remains below -60
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES keeps increasing for two weeks but RETAIL_REC stays flat or declines over the following four weeks, the lagged catch-up mechanism is rejected.
